newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo central banker says no need to devalue - agency.
newsitem.headline: Yugo central banker says no need to devalue - agency.

text.p: There is no reason to devalue the Yugoslav dinar, central bank deputy governor Bozidar Gazivoda was reported by the state news agency Tanjug as saying on Tuesday.

"The months-long monetary stability as a result of firm control of all monetary aggregates and the increase in hard currency reserves are the basic argument in defending the existing exchange rate," Tanjug quoted Gazivoda as saying.
National Bank officials were not immediately available for comment on the report.

Exporters keen to improve their position on foreign markets have been arguing for a weaker dinar, while independent economists from the Institute for Economic Sciences have called for a floating exchange rate.

Gazivoda, who has headed the central bank since the federal parliament dismissed former governor Dragoslav Avramovic in May, said the current exchange rate reflected the real relationship between domestic and world market prices.
The dinar's black market value has stabilized at 3.4 dinars to the mark, compared with the official rate of 3.3 dinars.
The central bank last devalued the dinar by almost 70 percent in November 1995 to bring it in line with the then black market rate.
The economists say rising inflation, which reached a rate of 99.2 percent in the year to August, is increasing pressure on the current exchange rate.

At the same time, analysts speculate the government may be forced to resort to printing cash to pay a growing backlog of wages owed to employees of state-owned companies. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
